definition: Premium crude is a grade of crude oil that yields a high proportion of lighter, more valuable products through simple distillation alone, and commands a higher price than lower-quality crude as a result.
core_idea: Because the actual product mix from crude oil varies by source, crude that naturally distills into a high share of light (valuable) products is labeled premium and priced higher than crude lacking that composition.
key_points: Every barrel of crude oil contains a different underlying mix of raw materials, so actual refined output varies substantially from the 'typical' mix.
Premium crude converts into a high proportion of lighter products via simple distillation.
Premium crude oils are priced higher than lower-quality crude oil.
relationships: Premium crude designation relates to, but is described separately from, the light/heavy (API gravity) and sweet/sour classifications
trading_implications: Crude grade differentials in pricing partly reflect how 'premium' (light-product-rich) a given crude's natural distillation yield is.
